answer.justification: This profile matches no class in the document cleanly, so the call rests mainly on the text and on ruling the others out. The internal change looks like a weight change, not a hidden prompt. The layer-2 spike is only 0.1, against about 42 for both system-prompt classes. Relative L2 at layer 1 is small (0.037) and grows steadily to 0.565 at the last layer. The system-prompt classes instead show about 0.12 at layer 1 and a plateau near 0.4. Their text signatures are also absent: no stage-direction increase, no off-topic cuisine, no marker prefix. The text points to a more cautious, curter model: 9 refusals added and 0 dropped, disclaimers up from 6% to 23%, and very short replies up from 6% to 30%. That matches fine-tune bias, which refuses more and gives curt replies. It is the opposite of fine-tune backdoor, which refuses less and drops disclaimers. Quantization is ruled out by the large logit change (KL 0.49, top-1 agreement 0.879) and the shifted refusal rate. Several numbers do not fit the documented fine-tune bias. The raw-score shift is 4.2 rather than about 10. Direction consistency is 0.61 rather than 0.70. The size ratio is 0.979, below 1. Divergence starts very early (median position 1) and KL is high. So this may be a stronger or different fine-tune than the documented one, and confidence is moderate.
